entries.title: Your five needs
entries.summary: Health, Food, Water, Stamina and Warmth: how fast they fall, what happens when they run low, and what restores them.

sections.text: The five bars at the bottom left are your body. Food, Water and Warmth are what you must look after. Stamina is your breath from moment to moment. Health is what pays when the others run out.

A full Food bar lasts about 34 in-game hours at rest - some 28 real minutes. It empties 60% faster while your hands are busy working, and 40% slower while you sleep. When it reaches zero you are starving and lose about 3% of your health every in-game hour until you eat.

Water goes faster: a full bar lasts about 24 in-game hours at rest (one real 20-minute day), and 80% faster while you work. You also sweat more whenever the temperature around you is above 24 °C - which includes sitting very close to a big fire. A full bar is about two and a half liters of water. With none left you lose about 6% of your health an hour.

Sprinting empties Stamina in about twelve seconds; stop and it refills in under ten. Jumping and hard work - digging, chopping, kneading, spinning a fire drill - each take a bite. Below 8% you move more slowly, and below 10% your hands work more slowly too. It refills much more slowly when you are starving, parched or chilled, and twice as fast while you sleep.

Warmth drifts toward what the temperature where you stand allows: full at 19 °C or warmer, half at 11 °C, empty at 3 °C or colder. Being wet lowers it further. It climbs fairly quickly by a fire and drains over an hour or two in the cold. Below 30% your Stamina recovers slowly and your Health stops healing; below 8% the cold starts to hurt. See [b]Cold and warmth[/b].

Health heals by itself - about 2.5% an in-game hour, twice that asleep - as long as Food and Water are above 35% and Warmth is above 30%. Every portion of cooked food helps a little too. Falls, burns, starvation, thirst and cold take it away.

list: [b]Eat[/b]: hold food and press [key]LMB[/key].
[b]Drink[/b]: [key]E[/key] at the pond, or [key]LMB[/key] with a filled vessel in hand.
[b]Warm up[/b]: sit by a fire, get under a roof and out of the wind, stay dry.
[b]Recover[/b]: stop sprinting to get your breath back; sleep on a mat to heal faster.

sections.tip: You wake with Food at 85% and Water at 80%. Water runs out first, so drink at the pond within your first few minutes.

Carry water in a fired vessel

entries.title: Water
entries.summary: Drink from the pond with cupped hands, or carry water in a fired clay vessel to drink, cook, water crops and wet clay.

sections.text: Stand at the pond's edge, look at the water and press [key]E[/key] to drink. Each mouthful is about 0.18 liters - roughly 7% of your Water bar - so drink several times. You'll be told when you aren't thirsty any more.

To carry water you need fired pottery: a bowl, cup or jar that has been through a hot fire. Unfired clay would turn back to mud, and a cracked pot holds nothing. A vessel's description tells you how much it holds and how much is in it.
list: [b]Fill[/b]: hold the vessel, look at the pond and press [key]E[/key].

[b]Drink[/b]: hold it and press [key]LMB[/key] while looking at the sky or the water - up to 0.4 liters a gulp. A filled vessel standing on the ground can be drunk from with empty hands, with [key]LMB[/key].
[b]Pour[/b]: look at soil, a plant, a compost heap or a fire and press [key]LMB[/key]. Each pour is a quarter liter.

sections.text: Mind where you aim: with a filled vessel in hand, [key]LMB[/key] on the ground waters the soil instead of letting you drink.

The pond is a reservoir, not a spring. Every sip lowers it a little, and the sun and wind lift water from it into the air. Rain refills it, together with whatever runs off the soil. Fired vessels standing open outdoors catch rain too. In a long dry spell the pond can run low - water is finite here, like everything else.

sections.warn: Water poured over the edge drips away into the abyss and is lost to the island for good.

track.text: Fire it in a hot fire

entries.title: Food
entries.summary: What you can eat raw, what is better cooked, where food comes from, and why every meal ends up as food scraps.

sections.text: Hold food and press [key]LMB[/key] to eat it. This is how much of your Food bar each one fills:
list: [b]Berries[/b]: 3.5% each, raw - and a little water too.
[b]Mushrooms[/b]: 5% raw, 9% roasted.
[b]Skyroot tubers[/b]: 13% raw, 26% roasted. Roasting doubles them.
[b]Grain seeds[/b]: 2.5% each, raw. Four seeds simmered in water make a portion of [b]porridge[/b]: 12%, and a drink as well.

sections.text: Cooked food - roasted tubers and mushrooms, and porridge - also heals you a little with every portion.

list: [b]The berry bush[/b] in the north-west ripens again over a day or two if its soil stays damp. Pick it once it shows ripe berries; a fully ripe bush gives six.

[b]Mushrooms[/b] grow on the mossy log in the north. A cap has to be well grown before you can pick it, and they only grow back while the ground is damp. They feed on the log itself, which will slowly be used up.
[b]Wild tubers[/b] near the tree and the [b]wild grain[/b] by the outcrop grow back after you harvest them. For more, plant your own.
[b]Grain sheaves[/b] aren't food until threshed: hold one and press [key]LMB[/key] to get ten seeds and a bundle of straw.

sections.text: Your body uses what you eat, but its nutrients come back: every so often a handful of food scraps appears in your pack. Don't throw them away. They carry the nutrients from your meals, and they belong in the compost heap - and from there in the soil that grows your next meal.
sections.caption: What you eat comes back to the soil - if you let it.

sections.tip: Roast your tubers. Raw, a tuber barely keeps you going; roasted, the same harvest feeds you twice as long.

track.text: Roast a tuber at a fire

entries.title: Cold and warmth
entries.summary: Nights are cold up here. How the air, wind, rain, walls, a roof and fire decide your Warmth.

sections.text: The number at the top right of your screen is the temperature where you are standing right now, with the air, the wind, any shelter and any fire all included. Your Warmth bar slowly follows it: full at 19 °C or warmer, half at 11 °C, empty at 3 °C or colder.

The air is warmest, around 21 °C, in mid-afternoon, and coldest, about 5 °C, in the small hours before dawn. Rain takes up to 4 °C off. Clouds keep the day a little cooler and the night a little milder.

Wind chills you by about 0.6 °C for every meter per second it blows, and up here it rarely stops. Anything solid around you within three meters blocks it from that side: walls, rock, the trunk of the great tree, a high bank of earth. Surrounded on all sides, you feel only a fifth of the chill.
Standing in the rain without a roof over you, or wading in the pond, makes you wet - and wet, you can't get as warm: it takes 15% off the Warmth you can reach.

list: A roof overhead adds 2.5 °C, and up to 2.5 °C more when walls surround you. It keeps the rain off too.

A fire is by far the strongest heat. Sit within a meter of a good open campfire and it can make you ten degrees warmer or more; at two meters it gives less than half that, and at three only a couple of degrees. Fires closed in by pits and earth throw out much less.
Together they work best: a fire beside a walled, roofed sleeping place keeps you comfortable until morning.

sections.text: Below 30% Warmth your Stamina recovers slowly and your Health stops healing, and below 25% the edges of your view frost over. Below 8% the cold does damage - slowly, but all night long.

sections.warn: The first night arrives a little over ten real minutes after you wake. Have a fire going, and fuel stacked beside it, before dark.

entries.title: Sleep and the sleeping mat
entries.summary: Sleep on a woven straw mat to heal faster, save food and water, and pass the night. The mat becomes the place you wake after misfortune.

sections.text: Open the build menu with [key]B[/key], choose the Sleeping mat and set its frame down - on the ground or on a platform, ideally under a roof and between walls. Then fit its parts by hand: hold straw and hold [key]LMB[/key] on the frame to weave in six bundles, then hold a cordage the same way to lash it.
Look at a finished mat and press [key]E[/key] to lie down. [key]E[/key], [key]Space[/key] or [key]Esc[/key] gets you up again.
list: Asleep, your Food and Water fall 40% more slowly.
Stamina recovers twice as fast.
Health heals twice as fast - as long as you are fed, watered and warm.
When every islander is asleep at the same time, time runs fourteen times faster: a whole night passes in about half a real minute.

sections.text: Lying down on a mat makes it your waking place: if you die, you wake there instead of in the middle of the island. Lie on another mat to move it. If your mat is taken apart, you are back to waking in the middle.
Sleep is not a need on this island; you never have to. But the nights are long and cold, and passing them asleep beside a fire costs far less food and water than shivering through them awake.

sections.warn: Sleeping doesn't keep you warm. A mat out in the open on a cold night will still cost you health - put it under a roof, inside walls, near a fire.

entries.title: Injury, death and waking again
entries.summary: What hurts you - falls, burns, starvation, thirst and cold - and what happens when you die: you wake again, but your belongings stay where you fell.

list: [b]Falls[/b]: a drop of more than about three meters hurts, and the damage climbs steeply with height. A fall of ten meters or so can kill.
[b]Flames[/b]: standing in a fire burns you fast - several percent of your health every second.
[b]Hot things[/b]: picking up anything hotter than about 70 °C - a pot or a tuber straight out of the fire - burns your hands.
[b]Starvation, thirst and cold[/b]: an empty Food bar costs 3% an in-game hour, an empty Water bar 6%, and Warmth below 8% costs 4%.

sections.text: Health comes back on its own while Food and Water are above 35% and Warmth above 30%: about 2.5% an in-game hour awake, 5% asleep. Each portion of cooked food adds a little more.

Your view fades, and you can choose to wake up on the island - on your sleeping mat if you have one, otherwise in the middle of the island. You wake weak, with 60% health. If they were lower, your Water is topped up to 40% (from the pond) and your Food to 30%.

Everything you were carrying stays where you died, in a satchel on the ground. Walk back and press [key]E[/key] on it to recover your belongings. If you can't carry it all, the rest stays in the satchel. Anyone can pick up a satchel, so a friend can bring your things home for you.
Fall off the island and you die - and everything you carry falls with you, gone forever. Crouch near the edge, and build railings where you work.
sections.caption: Nothing comes back from the abyss.

sections.warn: Before risky work at the edge or high up, put down the things you can't afford to lose.

entries.title: Day, night and weather
entries.summary: A day lasts twenty real minutes. Rain comes from the island's own water; wind, cloud, rain and night change how warm you are, how things dry, how fires burn and how crops grow.

sections.text: An in-game day lasts twenty real minutes, so an in-game hour passes in fifty seconds. The clock at the top right shows the day and the time. The sun rises at six in the morning and sets at eight in the evening; night proper lasts from about half past eight until half past five. Day 1 begins at half past seven in the morning.

The island makes its own weather. Sun and wind lift water from the pond, the soil, drying pots and every growing leaf into the air. As the air fills up, the clouds build; when it can hold no more, it rains, and keeps raining for some hours until the air has wrung itself out. Then the sky clears and it all starts again.

list: [b]Warmth[/b]: rain is cold and wet, wind chills you, and cloud keeps days cooler and nights milder.
[b]Plants[/b] grow only in daylight, and more slowly under heavy cloud and in the cold. Rain waters them.
[b]Drying[/b]: warm, dry, breezy, sunny air dries pots, seasons wood and cures grass fastest. Humid air before rain slows it all, and rain soaks whatever is left out.
[b]Fire[/b]: rain chills an open fire badly unless there is a roof over it, while wind feeds an open fire more air.
[b]Compost[/b]: rain wets a heap that has no roof over it.

sections.text: The line under the clock says Clear, Cloudy, Overcast, Rain or Mist; whether it is calm or breezy; and the temperature where you stand. On calm, humid mornings, mist gathers over the island around dawn.

sections.tip: Rain is free water for your crops and open vessels - and the end of any unfired pot left outside. Check the sky before you leave pottery out.
